title: Chrono-atlas of cell-type specific daily gene expression rhythms in the regenerating colon
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76318-5

How tissues maintain circadian rhythms during regeneration remains poorly understood. Here, the authors generate a 24-hour single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the regenerating mouse colon and show that cells dynamically adapt their circadian programs in a cell-, region-, and injury-dependent manner.

title: Anionic solvation reconstruction stabilizes interfacial chemistry for high-temperature and high-voltage Li metal batteries
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76363-0

High-temperature Li metal batteries are limited by low interfacial stability. Here, the authors utilize an anionic solvation reconstruction strategy to design a compact solvation structure electrolyte, which concurrently elevates thermal stability and stabilizes electrode–electrolyte interphase.

title: Acoustic higher-order topological metals with bound corner states in the continuum
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76445-z

Higher-order topology has been well established in insulators and semimetals. Here, authors evidence higher-order topology in metallic systems, and unveil a type of topological corner states that are naturally embedded in the bulk continuum with no need for intentional engineering.

title: Collective problem decomposition improves the wisdom of deliberative crowds
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76365-y

Consensus estimates from small groups are more accurate than pooled individual estimates, yet what drives this is unclear. Here, the authors show that breaking down the problem and reasoning together is key, surpassing aggregation of initial guesses.

title: Racialized economic concentration predicts storm-related injuries and deaths in the United States, 2005–2022
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76111-4

Extreme storms increasingly threaten public health across the United States. This study found that counties with greater racialized economic disadvantage experienced markedly higher rates of storm-related injuries and deaths.

title: Atomically dispersed Ti on MnOx-Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> tailors O 2p orbitals for CO oxidation and H<sub>2</sub>O/SO<sub>2</sub> resistance
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76406-6

Transition-metal oxides offer a low-cost alternative to precious metals for environmental catalysis, yet CO oxidation under humid and sulfur-laden conditions remains a challenge due to rapid catalyst poisoning. Here, the authors report an atomic dispersion of Ti-decorated MnOx-Fe2O3 catalyst with excellent activity and resistance to poisoning.

title: The inherent capacity of neurons to learn order relations and support abstract reasoning
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 05 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76102-5

How the brain learns relations between objects and concepts remains largely unclear. Here, the authors show that a simple synaptic plasticity rule can achieve this and enable abstract inference, reconfiguration, and the emergence of cognitive maps in shallow networks.
